| **1**                                                                                                                                | **Step 0: Intent Selector** (“What do you need from this meeting?”) **Function**: The user picks what kind of clarity they need. This personalises the structure. **Options (4-tile menu):** _Pitch an idea_ → structure focuses on benefits \+ next steps _Update stakeholders_ → structure focuses on key facts \+ status _Defend a decision_ → structure focuses on rationale \+ risk _Ask smart questions_ → structure focuses on context \+ 2–3 sharp questions **Visuals** Four horizontal tiles with icons (lightbulb, bar chart, shield, question mark). Subtle hover glow; microcopy under each (e.g., “Turn your idea into a sharp 30-sec pitch”). Colour accents: Pitch \= warm amber Update \= teal Defend \= deep blue Questions \= violet **Step 1: Fog Flush (30–40 sec)** Progress Bar Note: In Figma, Fog Flush is shown as dot 2 of 7 in the step indicator (Step 0 \= dot 1, Fog Flush \= dot 2). The requirement doc labels steps starting from "Step 1" but the Figma top bar starts counting from Step 0\. Dev implement: 7 dots total for Executive Clarity Protocol. Step 0 activates dot 1; each subsequent step activates the next dot. **Function:** Quick state shift from scattered → focused using breath \+ visual. **Mechanics** Simple 4–2–4 breathing ratio (inhale 4, hold 2, exhale 4\) for \~5 cycles. Note: The breathing ratio (4-2-4) is always fixed and does NOT change based on the duration selected (3/5/10 min). The Fog Flush step always runs exactly 5 breath cycles at the 4-2-4 ratio, regardless of the total session duration chosen. Duration selection controls overall session length only, not this step. Central circle that: Expands on inhale (brightens) Pauses on hold (locks) Shrinks \+ softens on exhale **Visuals** Background slightly blurred at the start, gradually sharpens as breaths complete → literal “fog clearing” effect. Note: This blur-to-clear animation is unique to Boardroom Mode and is NOT the same as the standard breathing orb used in Bloom or Serenique. The background blur begins at \~8–10px and decreases progressively across the 5 breath cycles, reaching 0 blur by cycle 5\. Breathing shape uses concentric rings (Figma node 916:2197 — 3 concentric ellipses: 173px, 146px, 113px). Haptics: HapticFeedback.trigger("impactLight") on inhale start; HapticFeedback.trigger("impactMedium") on exhale. Optional — user can toggle haptics off. Tiny text at bottom: “Clearing mental fog… 3 breaths left.” **Step 2: Idea Capture** (“Say it messy”) (30–45 sec) Note: The 30–45 sec timer is app-driven and counts down automatically. Users can proceed early by tapping "Next" (confirmed in Figma). The timer is a guide, not a hard block. Voice input uses native OS Speech-to-Text (no AI, no external API). **Function:** The user brain-dumps what they’re trying to say. No pressure to be polished. **Mechanics** After Fog Flush, screen text: “In one go, put down what you’re trying to get across in this meeting. Don’t worry about wording.” The user can either type what they want to say or have the option of using the microphone. **Step 3: 3-Block Map** (Point – Proof – Payoff) (45–60 sec) **Function:** The user breaks down their idea in a 3 point, articulate message. **Mechanics** Screen text: “Break down your idea into 3 parts. This will help clear the noise and help articulate your thoughts better.” **Point** → main message **Proof** → supporting data/example **Payoff** → why it matters / next step The screen shows three cards stacked vertically. Users can quickly edit any line (tap to type or re-record that block). Note (Phase 1, rule-based — NO AI): The Point / Proof / Payoff cards are pre-populated from the Idea Capture text entered in Step 2\. The system applies rule-based text splitting to map the brain-dump into the 3 fields. Voice recording from Step 2 is first transcribed via native OS Speech-to-Text, then treated as plain text for pre-population. Users can tap any field to edit after pre-population. **Visuals** Card layout with clear labels: Card 1: “POINT” (bold, maybe amber accent) Card 2: “PROOF” (teal) Card 3: “PAYOFF” (green) Simple microcopy above: “Here’s your idea in 3 moves. Tap to tweak.” **Step 4: Laser Sentence** (20–30 sec) **Function:** Create one crystal-clear sentence they can open within the meeting.**Laser Sentence generation logic (Phase 1, rule-based, no AI):** The app constructs the sentence using a template based on the **Intent selected in Step 0** \+ the **Point from the 3-Block Map**: **Intent** **Template** Pitch "I'd like to propose \[Point\] because it can \[Payoff\] in \[timeframe\]." Update "Here's where we are on \[Point\]: \[Proof\], \[next step\]." Defend "We chose \[Point\] because \[Proof\], which best protects against \[Payoff\]." Questions "Before we decide, I want to clarify \[Point\] so we don't miss \[Payoff\]." The system string-injects the user's 3-Block Map content into these fixed templates. No AI needed in Phase 1\. **Mechanics** App auto-generates an opening line tailored to the Intent from Step 0\. For _Pitch_: **“I’d like to propose \[X\] because it can \[Y outcome\] in \[Z timeframe\].**” For _Update_: “Here’s where we are on \[project\]: \[status\], \[key risk\], \[next step\].” For _Defend_: “We chose \[option\] because \[rationale\], which best protects us against \[risk\].” For _Questions_: “Before we decide, I want to clarify a few things about \[area\] so we don’t miss \[risk/opportunity\].” Users can swipe through 2–3 alternative phrasings: “More concise / More diplomatic / More assertive”. Note: Swipe is MANUAL only — not automatic. The user swipes left/right to see the 3 tonal variants (Concise / Bold / Neutral). These are pre-generated using the same rule-based template at different lengths/tones. No auto-rotation. The pill buttons (Concise                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Neutral           | Bold) below the sentence also allow tapping to switch — confirmed in Figma. **Visuals** Large text in the centre (“Your Laser Sentence”). Small pill buttons below: “Concise”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | “Neutral”                | “Bold” Note: The Concise / Neutral / Bold buttons control the TONE and LENGTH of the Laser Sentence text — NOT font family or typography. Font stays consistent with the app design system throughout. Tap to copy → tiny toast: “Saved to clipboard”. Note — Two distinct copy/action icons on this screen (confirmed in Figma): 1\. Copy icon on the Laser Sentence card → copies ONLY the Laser Sentence to clipboard. 2\. "Send to myself" button (Step 6\) → sends the full session summary (Breath Pattern \+ Structure \+ Laser Sentence) via native OS share sheet (React Native Share.share()). **Step 5: Mental Rehearsal Flash** (20–30 sec) **Function:** Lock it into memory so it comes out smoothly under pressure. **Mechanics** The app shows the Laser Sentence and 3-Block Map in a minimal overlay. 2 quick run-throughs: The user reads the Laser Sentence silently once while a soft metronome ticks (pace). The user is nudged: “Now say your opening line out loud once.” "Whisper Mode" — UI text hint only (not a feature toggle). Displayed as static microcopy: "In an open office? Just whisper it." No microphone, no recording, no OS permission required. **Visuals** Clean black background, off-white text. Very subtle timer ring at top (counting down from 30 sec). At the end, the sentence gently fades, leaving just: “You’re ready.” **Step 6: Save \+ Quick Access** Figma Divergence — Use Figma (node 944:1127) as source of truth for Phase 1: • Figma shows: session summary card (Breath Pattern \+ Structure \+ Laser Sentence, each with a copy icon) \+ "Send to myself" button \+ "End Session" button. • "Pin to Boardroom Mode Home" described in this requirement doc is NOT present in Figma. • ACTION: Raise "Pin" feature with Product Owner — defer to Phase 2 or update Figma first before building. **Function:** Make it useful in real life (not just in-app) for last-second glances. **Mechanics** App offers: “Pin to Boardroom Mode Home” (for meetings in the next hour). “Send Laser Sentences to me via email/text” (one-tap share). **Visuals** Two big buttons: Note: "Pin for this meeting" is NOT present in Figma — defer to Phase 2\. Implement "Send to myself" only for Phase 1\. ~~“Pin for this meeting”~~ “Send to myself” Tiny reassurance copy: “Your notes are private and only stored on your device/secure server (copy for later).”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |     |

|                                                                                                                                      | **Pressure-Proof Presence → for confidence, presence, and sounding authoritative.** | **2**                                                                                                                                | **Step 0: State Selector** (“How do you want to show up?”) **Function:** The user chooses the _type_ of presence they need based on context. Options (4 modes): **Grounded** → calm, composed, emotionally regulated **Authoritative** → strong delivery, firm tone **Warm** → human, relatable, approachable **Neutral \- Professional** → steady, controlled, balanced Each mode triggers a specific breath \+ vocal pattern. Visuals Four tiles: Grounded → deep green gradient Authoritative → charcoal with gold highlight Warm → soft amber Neutral → cool teal Hover ripple \+ subtle micro-pulse Tiny sublines: Grounded: _“Stop the adrenaline spike.”_ Authoritative: _“Stabilise tone. Command the room.”_ Warm: _“Speak like a human.”_ Neutral: _“Controlled \+ clear.”_ **Step 1: CEO Breath** (40–60 sec) Progress Bar Note: CEO Breath \= dot 2 of 6 in Figma progress bar (State Selector \= dot 1, CEO Breath \= dot 2). Doc labels this "Step 1" but Figma progress bar counts Step 0 \= dot 1\. Figma is correct — 6 dots total for Pressure-Proof Presence. **Function:** Immediately shifts the user from sympathetic (“fight/flight”) → parasympathetic (“calm control”). This stabilises: heart rate voice vibration breathing patterns jaw muscles Mechanics Screen layout (confirmed Figma node 980:1968): Glowing orb at center (213×213px with nested ellipses for glow). Top shows breathing ratio in large text (e.g., "5                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 0                 | 5" for Authoritative mode) \+ "Inhale • Hold • Exhale" label. Jaw / shoulder / spine / feet instructions appear as sequential text prompts during breath cycles — no separate UI elements required for them. App uses breathing ratios depending on mode: Grounded → 4-2-6 Authoritative → 5-0-5 (slow, even breathing \= vocal power) Warm → 3-2-4 (softer exhale) Neutral → 4-4 box (equilibrium) Visual at centre: A glowing orb expands/contracts in sync with breathing. Haptics: single tap \= inhale Note: The horizontal bar visible in Figma on this and other steps is a READ-ONLY progress indicator — NOT a user-draggable slider. Implement as an animated fill bar that progresses over the step duration. long pulse \= exhale Visuals Orb glows brighter on inhale, dims on exhale Background blur clears gradually Text shifts from “Tension detected” → “Stability restored” **Step 2: Body-Set Alignment** (40 sec) **Function:** Corrects posture, reduces fidgeting, releases shoulder tension → All essential for looking calm and sounding confident. **Mechanics** A silhouette or outline on screen guides 4 micro-adjustments: **Jaw Unlock** – “Drop your jaw by 2–3 mm, unclench teeth.” **Shoulder Reset** – “Roll shoulders back \+ down once.” **Spine Lift** – “Imagine a string pulling the back of your head up.” **Feet Anchor** – “Place both feet flat. Feel the weight evenly spread.” Each step takes 8–10 seconds. Visuals Simple silhouette with glowing nodes at jaw, shoulders, spine, feet Each node lights up as the user completes the step Node behavior (confirmed Figma node 981:2600): Nodes auto-advance on a TIMER — no user tap required. Each node glows gold for its instruction duration (\~8–10 sec). After the timer elapses, the next node activates automatically. Dev implement: array of 4 steps × 8–10 sec timer; highlight corresponding node on each tick. Soft vibration confirms step completion — triggered when each step timer elapses (not on user tap). Use HapticFeedback.trigger("notificationSuccess"). No camera or motion detection required. The Body-Set Alignment screen shows a **human silhouette** (confirmed in Figma — vector outline 198×466px). On it are **6 circular node hotspots** at jaw, shoulders (×2), spine, feet (×2). These nodes **sequentially illuminate** — each one glows gold when its instruction is shown (e.g., jaw node lights up when "Jaw Unlock" instruction is displayed). After \~8–10 seconds, the next node activates. **This is a timer-driven sequential highlight — no user tap required.** The nodes auto-advance. Dev implement: array of 4 steps × 8–10 sec timer, highlight the corresponding node position on each step tick. **Step 3: Vocal Power Prime** (30–40 sec) Progress Bar Note: Vocal Power Prime \= dot 4 of 6 in Figma (doc "Step 3" \= Figma dot 4). Figma is correct. **Function:** Removes shaky voice, breathiness, and “smallness”. Gives the user: stable vocal cords slower speech rhythm confident resonance **Mechanics** The app plays a low-frequency hum (100–150 Hz). The user hums along for 5–7 seconds at a time. Sound Assets Required (Content team action): 3 pre-recorded audio files (MP3/AAC): Chest Resonance \~100 Hz | Mouth Resonance \~130 Hz | Head Resonance \~150 Hz. These are static files, NOT synthesised at runtime. Three rounds: **Chest Resonance** (low hum) **Mouth Resonance** (mid-tone) **Head Resonance** (lighter hum) Visuals Rings emanate from a centre point in sync with the hum User's resonance visualised as a waveform (simple, not diagnostic) — this is a STATIC ANIMATION only. 12 vertical bars animate in a wave pattern synced to audio playback (Figma node 981:2679). Does NOT use microphone. Does NOT measure actual voice. No microphone permission required for this step. After each hum: “Tone stabilising…” “Voice steady.” Text for the 3 Vocal Power Prime rounds: **Round** **Screen Label** **Instruction Text** Round 1 Chest Resonance "Hum low and deep. Feel vibrations in your chest cavity." Round 2 Mouth Resonance "Raise the tone slightly. Feel resonance in your mouth." Round 3 Head Resonance "Lighten the tone. Feel the vibration move toward your head." After each: "Tone stabilising…" → "Voice steady." (as per requirement doc) **Step 4: Presence Lock-In** (20–30 sec) **Function:** Final micro-prime that locks in the behavioural shift so it carries into the meeting. **Mechanics** The user sees 3 rapid-fire identity prompts depending on their mode choice. Mechanics detail: 3 sentences appear SEQUENTIALLY — one at a time, each for \~3 seconds with soft fade-in. The screen shows a 30-second countdown ring at top (Figma confirmed). Background slowly brightens over 30 seconds. After all 3 sentences: auto-advance to Snapshot screen. No user input required during this step. **Grounded Mode** “You lead with calm.” “Slow breath, steady tone.” “Nothing shakes you.” **Authoritative Mode** “Your voice carries weight.” “You hold the room.” “Speak with certainty.” **Warm Mode** “You connect easily.” “Your tone is human.” “People lean in.” **Neutral Mode** “Centered.” “Precise.” “Professional presence.” The user reads each silently for 3 seconds as the screen slowly brightens. Visuals Soft fade-in text Clean background Progress ring at top shrinking from 20 → 0 seconds **Step 5: Snapshot \+ Quick Access Function:** Stores the user’s calibrated state and gives a one-tap fast reset before the meeting. **Mechanics User gets a summary card showing:** **Breath pattern** **Posture cue** **Vocal anchor line** **“Save for this meeting” button pins it to Boardroom Mode Home.** **One-tap “15-sec Reset” button launches a compressed version.** **Visuals Card with tiny icons (breath / posture / hum)** **Button colour reflects original mode (green, gold, amber, teal)** **Microcopy: “You’re in Presence Mode.”** Figma Divergence (Figma node 981:3817) — Use Figma as source of truth for Phase 1: • Figma shows: summary card (Selected Mode, Breath Pattern, Key Posture Cue, Vocal Anchor — each row with copy icon) \+ "15-sec Reset" button \+ "End Session" button. • "Save for this meeting" pinning described in req doc is NOT in Figma — defer to Phase 2\. • "15-sec Reset" \= compressed 15-second version of CEO Breath only. |     |

| **3**                                                                                                                                | **Rapid Intelligence Filter → for high-pressure Q\&A, unexpected challenges, and moments where you must sound intelligent instantly.** |                                                                                                                                      | **Step 0: Response Mode Selector** (“What situation are you preparing for?”) User picks the type of thinking challenge: Progress Bar Note: Rapid Intelligence Filter uses 6 dots total. Response Mode Selector (Step 0 in doc) \= dot 1 in Figma. Same convention across all Boardroom toolkits: Step 0 \= dot 1 always. **Smart Answer** → turn any question into a structured reply **Challenge Response** → respond calmly when pushed, questioned, or doubted **Layman Translation** → simplify complex ideas for non-experts **Concise Summary** → reduce long explanations into 2–3 crisp lines **Visuals:** Four tiles: Smart Answer → navy with a spark icon Challenge Response → deep red with shield Layman Translation → green with leaf/spark Concise Summary → gold with slider icon Gentle hover glow \+ micro-ripples Subtitle under each tile explaining what it helps with. **Step 1: Cognitive Speed Primer** (25–30 sec) Progress Bar Note: Cognitive Speed Primer \= dot 2 of 6 in Figma (Figma node 1003:3130). Screen shows a large geometric shape at center with a timer bar at bottom. _A rapid-switching exercise that wakes up the prefrontal cortex._ **Function:** Increases cognitive speed, working memory, and verbal fluidity. **Mechanics** The user watches a set of shapes flash on screen (circle → triangle → square). They tap when the shape repeats. UI Note: Dark background with bright geometric shapes (circle, triangle, square). Timer bar sliding across bottom. Subtle chime sound when user responds correctly. Text at top: "Warming up your executive circuits…". Tally shown at end: "Correct: X / Missed: X". **Shape display logic for Cognitive Speed Primer (Phase 1, rule-based):** Sequence: circle → triangle → square → circle → square → triangle → square → square (repeat) etc. **A shape "repeats" when the same shape appears consecutively** — user must tap when they see back-to-back same shape Show approximately **15–20 shapes** over 25–30 seconds (roughly 1.5 seconds per shape) Repeat events occur \~4–5 times per session Track: correct taps (shape actually repeated) and missed taps (repeated but not tapped) Display tally: "Correct: X / Missed: X" — confirmed in Figma **Visuals** Dark background, bright geometric shapes Timer bar sliding across bottom Subtle chime when user responds correctly Small text: _“Warming up your executive circuits…”_ **Step 2: Thought Structuring Engine** (35–45 sec) Progress Bar Note: Thought Structuring Engine \= dot 3 of 6 in Figma (node 1003:3272). This is a SELECTION screen — user picks one framework from the 4 options (SPEAR/LARA/CLEAR/SOS). The actual fill-in of each framework component happens on the following screen. _The heart of the toolkit._ **Function:** Turns chaotic thoughts into clean, sharp, structured answers using a live template. **Mechanics** The user chooses their preferred structure and uses these to type / speak to break down their ideas. **SPEAR Method (for Smart Answers)** **S**tatement **P**oint **E**vidence **A**ction **R**elevance **LARA Method (for Challenge Response)** **L**isten **A**cknowledge **R**eframe **A**nswer **CLEAR Method (for Explaining Simply)** **C**ore Idea **L**anguage Simplified **E**xample **A**nalogy **R**eturn to Message **SOS Method (for Concise Summaries)** **S**ignificance **O**bservation **S**tep-Forward **Visuals** User sees the structure appear as 4–5 small cards They speak one sentence per card App highlights the card as they talk **Step 3: Verbal Smart-Filter** (20–30 sec) Progress Bar Note: Verbal Smart-Filter \= dot 4 of 6 in Figma (node 1003:3479). **⚠️ CRITICAL PHASE 1 CONSTRAINT — AI is OUT OF SCOPE for Phase 1\.** The "AI rewrites in real-time" described below must be replaced with rule-based logic for Phase 1\. Phase 1 implementation: 1\. User speaks (10–20 seconds) → transcribed using NATIVE OS Speech-to-Text (no AI, no external API calls). 2\. Rule-based filler removal: strip predefined filler words \["um", "uh", "basically", "so", "like", "kind of", "maybe", "sort of"\] from the transcription. 3\. "Smart Version" \= transcribed text with fillers stripped \+ proper capitalisation applied. No vocabulary elevation, no logic tightening in Phase 1\. 4\. The split-screen "Your Version" vs "Smart Version" still shows as designed — Smart Version \= filler-stripped output only. **⚠️ ACTION REQUIRED: Confirm with Product Owner whether filler-stripping alone is sufficient for Phase 1 MVP, or whether this entire step should be deferred to Phase 2 when AI is available.** **Function:** Removes unnecessary filler \+ makes the answer sound intelligent. Phase 1 (rule-based, no AI): The system applies filler-word removal to the transcribed text. Phase 2 will introduce AI rewriting including: removing filler words, tightening logic, strengthening verbs, simplifying syntax, elevating vocabulary subtly (without sounding pretentious). removing filler words tightening logic strengthening verbs simplifying syntax elevating vocabulary subtly (without sounding pretentious) **Output example:** User: _“Umm so basically what I’m trying to say is I think the data shows we could maybe improve retention slightly…”_ AI Smart-Filtered: **“The data indicates a clear opportunity to improve retention by focusing on X and Y.” Visuals:** Split-screen: “Your Version” vs “Smart Version” Option to swap between “Concise”, “Neutral”, “Assertive” Note: In Phase 1, Concise / Neutral / Assertive \= rule-based variants of the filler-stripped text at different lengths. Full AI tonal variation is a Phase 2 feature. **Step 4: Cognitive Calm Lock** (25–30 sec) Progress Bar Note: Cognitive Calm Lock \= dot 5 of 6 in Figma (node 1003:3688). Breathing animation: 4-second inhale / 6-second exhale with a growing line pacing visual and integration progress bar. _A micro-reset so the thinking improvements stick._ **Function:** Integrates the cognitive work with a physiological downshift. **Mechanics** Slow 4-second inhale 6-second exhale Tiny growing line that helps pace the breath Text overlays: “Slow breath \= faster brain.” “Sharp mind, calm delivery.” This ensures their thinking stays calm under pressure. **Step 5: Quick-Access Response Card Function** Progress Bar Note: Quick-Access Response Card \= dot 6 of 6 in Figma — final step (node 1003:3876). Figma and req doc are aligned on this screen. Shows 4 output cards: Structured Answer, Smart Opener, Challenge-Proof, Layman Translation. Actions: Pin to Boardroom Mode, Copy, Rehearse. User receives: One structured answer One smart-sentence opener One challenge-proof response line One layman translation line (if chosen) Examples: **Smart Opener:** “Here’s the simplest way to think about it…” **Challenge-Proof:** “That’s a valid concern, here’s how I’m looking at it…” **Layman Version:** “In plain language, what this means is…” **Visuals:** A clean card with 2–3 key lines “Pin to Boardroom Mode” “Copy to clipboard” “Rehearse once” button |                   |

| **1**                                                                                                                                | **Perception to Creativity \- _“See clearly → think differently.”_** **Step 1: Perspective Flip – Ambiguous Visual Purpose:** Move from clarity → creativity by forcing the brain to see multiple interpretations. **Visual Mechanism:** Screen transitions to a single ambiguous image, e.g.: Duck/Rabbit, face/vase, old woman/young woman, rotating cube, etc. Smooth crossfade from illusion wheel to ambiguous shape, so it feels like one experience. **Flow: Prompt 1 – First Perception:** Text: “What do you see first?” Two buttons appear beneath the image (e.g., “Duck” / “Rabbit”), or generic: “Option A / Option B” with small icons. The user taps one. **Prompt 2 – Second Perception:** Text: “Now, tilt or rotate your phone slowly and look again.” Very subtle animation on the image (slight morph, brightness shift) to help them see the second interpretation. New text: “Can you see the other image too?” Buttons: “Yes, now I see both” / “Not yet” If “Not yet”, the app briefly outlines hint edges on the second form, then fades. **Micro-coaching text appears:** “The picture didn’t change. _You_ changed how you looked at it.” “Problems and ideas work the same way.” This completes the flexibility / creativity priming. |                                                                                                                                      | **Wave → binaural beats & brainwave entertainment playlists** | **2**                                                                                                                                | **Neural Rhythm Reset \- _Binaural beats & brainwave entertainment playlists to stabilise your “mental rhythm”._ Step 1:** State Selector – “What does your mind feel like right now?” 4-option menu, phrased in plain language so people don’t need to know brainwaves: **Overloaded** – “Too many tabs open, can’t switch off.” **Scattered** – “Jumping between tasks, hard to focus.” **Flat** – “Low energy, struggling to get started.” **Wired** – “Hyper-alert, jittery before something important.” When the user taps a state: The tile expands with a wave animation preview: **Overloaded →** choppy, noisy wave **Scattered →** broken, misaligned waves **Flat →** almost flat line with tiny ripples **Wired →** tight, high-frequency wave Under the hood, each state maps to a target entrainment band: State Target Band (suggested) Intended Effect Overloaded Theta–low Alpha (6–9 Hz) Calm \+ mental unclenching Scattered Mid Alpha (9–11 Hz) Smooth, sustained focus Flat Low–mid Beta (13–16 Hz) Gentle activation Wired Alpha–Gamma blend (10–40 Hz textures) Clear but grounded alertness Visuals: Each tile has its own colour gradient: Overloaded → deep indigo → muted violet Scattered → teal → cyan Flat → soft orange → warm gold Wired → electric blue → neon amber On press, a hover ripple runs across the tile like a mini wave. **Step 2:** Wave Visualiser – “Sync to the rhythm” This is the main entertainment screen where audio \+ visuals work together. Layout: Background: dark navy/charcoal. Centre: a horizontal waveform or circular “wave ring” moving in time with the playlist. A small pulse orb travels along the wave to mark the beat. Interaction: A prompt appears first: “Tap the screen in time with the wave for 10 seconds.” As the user taps: When taps are off-beat → waves look jagged, orb flickers. When taps start matching → the wave becomes smoother, orb glows steadily. This creates a feeling of “locking in” with the rhythm, not just passively listening. Mode-specific behaviour: Overloaded → longer, slower wave cycles; amplitude gently rising and falling. Scattered → wave starts fragmented, then visually “joins up” as sync improves. Flat → small amplitude grows slightly as energy increases. Wired → high-frequency shimmer that gradually widens into a more spacious, stable wave. **Step 3:** Audio \+ Haptic Layer – Binaural Entrainment Once tapping alignment is detected (or after 10 seconds), the toolkit shifts into entrainment mode: The binaural beat track fades up to a comfortable level. Optional ambient layer blends in per mode: Overloaded → soft rain / ocean noise. Scattered → gentle wind \+ subtle chimes. Flat → light drum pulse or soft synth arpeggio. Wired → low, grounding bass \+ airy top layer. Haptics: A light vibration on every main beat (or every few beats, so it doesn’t feel frantic). Longer, softer pulse at the end of each 4- or 8-beat cycle to mark phrasing — like a “paragraph break” in the rhythm. User controls: Toggles along the top or bottom: Visual ○ on/off Sound ○ on/off Haptic ○ on/off So someone can, for example, use _only visual \+ haptic_ in a quiet office. **Step 4:** Optional – Bioadaptive Wave (Phase 2+) If/when you integrate Apple Health / wearables, you can add: A small HR/HRV indicator in a corner. If HRV is low / heart rate high: The wave slows slightly, bass deepens, colours darken → more calming. If HRV is already good: Wave keeps a lighter texture, slightly faster tempo → maintenance, not sedation. Label it: “Adaptive Mode – adjusting waves to your nervous system.” (For now, this can just be “Coming soon” in the early build.) **Step 5:** Reflection Echo – “Lock in your new rhythm” After 2–5 minutes (or when the user hits “End Session”): The wave gradually flattens into a smooth, slow pulse. Audio fades to a soft single tone, then silence. Screen shifts to a gentle glow (same colour family as chosen state). Prompts: “How does your mind feel now?” with a simple 3-icon scale: Fuzzy → Clearer → Very Clear “What do you want to do next with this clarity?” with 3 quick actions: Start Focus Session (links straight into Clarity toolkit) Go into Creative Mode (links into Vision/Spark) Save this Wave (stores chosen preset \+ duration in a “My Waves” library) If saved, show a tiny visual thumbnail (mini waveform \+ colour) in their history.             |                   |

| **3**                                                                                                                                | **Clarity → deep work focus reset**                                       |                   |
|                                                                                                                                      | **Neural Focus Bands \*Colour scheme has to be dark, this toolkit would require camera access Screen copy: Neural Focus Bands**Build a deep, stable focus for high-stakes work in 2 minutes. You’ll:– Hold a steady touch on the Focus Anchor– Respond to tiny visual cues– Get a Focus Clarity Score at the end **\[Start Session\]** User taps **Start Session**. 1\. Calibration (5–10 seconds) **UI:** Background: dark, minimal Center/bottom: **Focus Anchor** (small circle) Top: short instructions **Prompt: Step 1 — Get Set**Hold your phone comfortably.Place your index finger on the circle and keep it there. When the user touches the anchor and the device stillness is acceptable: **Sub-prompt (fade in):** Great. Stay as still as is comfortable.We’re calibrating your focus signals. App quietly starts: front camera (for gaze \+ blink) accelerometer (stillness) baseline touch consistency After \~5–10 seconds of stable input → auto-advance. 2\. Main Focus Loop (90–120 seconds) Now we run the **real session**, in a repeating loop. 2.1 Base State **UI: Alignment Lines** visible (slightly moving / misaligned) Focus Anchor glowing softly under the user’s finger Very minimal text at top: **Focus Mode**Keep your eyes on the center of the screen.Keep your finger on the circle. **System continuously measures:** Eye fixation stability Blink rhythm Touch micro-consistency Device stillness Lines subtly adapt: Stable signals → lines cleaner, more aligned Unstable → lines drift, micro-shake increases _No extra prompts yet, just presence._ 2.2 Micro-Prompt: Reaction Time (every \~20–30s) **Event:**A tiny flash appears near the center (a small dot or micro-line). **Top prompt (appears 0.5s before first use):** When a small dot appears, tap it quickly while keeping your finger on the circle. **Behavior:** Dot appears briefly User taps anywhere (or on the dot) while keeping finger anchored App records reaction time & accuracy Dot disappears **If missed:**Subtle text: Missed that one — no problem. Stay with it. Then fade back to **Focus Mode** instructions only. 2.3 Micro-Prompt: Precision Tap (cognitive noise) Every 20–30 seconds (staggered from reaction prompts): **Event:**A **tiny disappearing dot** appears near the periphery. **Prompt (first time only):** When you see a faint dot at the edge, tap it as precisely as you can. App measures: Tap offset from dot position → **Tap Precision** Variability over time → cognitive noise Lines respond briefly: High precision → lines become sharper for \~2s Low precision → no change or slight drift 2.4 Passive Blink & Stillness Capture (continuous, no user action) No explicit prompt here (to keep it non-intrusive), but UX supports measurement: Every \~30–40s, screen luminance subtly dips/raises → helps detect blink rhythm Device stillness captured while finger is on anchor If the phone shakes significantly: **Soft prompt:** Try to rest the phone or your arm to reduce movement. Then return to base state. 3\. Adaptive Visual Feedback (always on) Throughout the session, the user sees **subtle, meaningful feedback**: **High stability** (good fixation, calm blinks, precise taps, still device): Lines align into neat geometry Contrast becomes clean Focus Anchor glows with a stable halo **Low stability** (drift, irregular blinks, jitter, sloppy taps): Lines break symmetry slightly Tiny jitter or waves appear Anchor halo pulses unevenly No big messages, just visually:“You are locked in” vs “You’re drifting.” 4\. Session End (after 90–120 seconds) **Fade out alignment lines.Show summary panel. Header: Focus Session Complete** Underneath, show **sub-metrics** as a simple list or radar: **Eye Fixation Stability:** High **Blink Rhythm:** Moderate (slightly irregular) \*\*\* these will require camera access **Tap Precision:** Strong **Touch Consistency:** High **Reaction-Time Stability:** High No score, just talk about **accuracy**\! For example- you were accurate with the taps, give the toolkit another go to make your eye fixation more stable. **Insights block:** You held stable focus for most of the session.Main drift signals came from hand movement and irregular blinking. Try resting your elbow or phone next time to stabilize more. **Buttons: \[Run Again — 2 min\] \[Use Focus Bands While Reading\]** (if you support integration mode) **\[Done\]** |                   |

|                                                                                                                                      | **Pattern Lens** Helps you see patterns and structure in information — the base of creativity and strategy. What it is: You are shown a clean, minimal set of visuals (like shapes, flows, or small data points).They reorganize in different ways.You identify the underlying structure. What the user sees: 9–12 elements arranged simply They move into new configurations Some movements suggest patterns (growth, cycles, sequences) The visual style is **calm, elegant**, like a well-designed consulting diagram coming alive. What the user does: Taps the moment they recognize a pattern Selects which pattern it is (trend, cycle, clustering, flow) Sometimes rearranges the elements to propose a clearer structure Why this makes sense: Human creativity emerges from recognizing unseen patterns.This tool literally trains that mechanism, without games or illusions. Output: **Pattern Recognition Signature** fast pattern finder structure-first meaning-first or detail-first |                                                                                                                                      | **CAFFEINE OPTIMIZATION TOOLKIT**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                   |
| **1**                                                                                                                                | A precision system for using caffeine to improve alertness, performance, and sleep. **SECTION 1 — USER INPUT SYSTEM: DRINK LIBRARY \+ LOGGING** **Purpose:** Allow users to input caffeine intake with accuracy and create a data foundation for all future recommendations. **1.1 Preloaded Drink Library (with estimated mg values)** These appear when a user taps **“Add Drink”:** **Coffee** Single espresso — 75 mg Double espresso — 150 mg Americano (small) — 95 mg Americano (medium) — 150 mg Americano (large) — 180 mg Cappuccino — 80 mg Latte — 80 mg Flat white — 90 mg Filter coffee (small) — 120 mg Filter coffee (medium) — 150 mg Filter coffee (large) — 200 mg Cold brew (standard) — 150 mg Cold brew (strong) — 220 mg Decaf coffee — 10 mg **Tea** Green tea — 30 mg Black tea — 50 mg Matcha (small) — 60 mg Matcha (large) — 80 mg White tea — 20 mg Herbal tea — 0 mg **Energy Drinks** Standard can (250 ml) — 80 mg Strong can (500 ml) — 160 mg **Soft Drinks** Cola — 34 mg Diet cola — 45 mg **User Custom Drink** Input fields: Name Drink type Size Caffeine amount (mg) Strength tag → Low / Medium / High **1.2 Logging Prompts (exact text)** When user logs a drink, show: **Prompt:** “Logged: \[Drink Name\] — \[X mg caffeine\].” Follow-up question (optional to user): “How did this drink make you feel?” Calm & focused Neutral Jittery Too strong Didn’t feel it (This feeds personalization.) **SECTION 2 — CAFFEINE TIMING ADVISOR** (Active every time user logs or requests guidance.) Core Logic Inputs Logged by User Wake time (first unlock) Time since wake Time to bedtime Total caffeine today Drink strength (mg) User-specific optimal window User sensitivity level Sleep quality last night Time since last drink **2.1 PROMPT SET A — "TOO EARLY AFTER WAKING" (0–60 min after wake)** **Trigger:** Drink logged or requested within 0–60 minutes after waking. **Rationale:** Caffeine interferes with cortisol awakening response. **Primary message:** “Your body is still in its natural morning alertness phase. Caffeine right now may give you a short boost but often causes jitter or a mid-morning crash.” **Supportive line:** “You’ll usually get a more stable performance boost if you wait about 45–60 minutes.” **Suggestions:** “Log this anyway” (for autonomy) “Remind me in 45 minutes to have caffeine” “Show me non-caffeine alertness options” **2.2 PROMPT SET B — OPTIMAL WINDOW (90–180 minutes after waking) Trigger:** Drink logged in optimal biological window. **Primary message:** “This is your strongest window for caffeine. Expect clearer focus and steadier energy.” **Secondary text:** “This timing aligns with natural adenosine patterns for optimal alertness.” **Suggestions:** “Good choice — log drink” “Recommendations for the rest of the day” “Set this as your typical morning drink” **2.3 PROMPT SET C — MIDDAY CAFFEINE (After 3.5 hours from last drink)** **Trigger:** User requests caffeine mid-morning before a meeting or energy lull. **Primary message:** “A moderate amount of caffeine now can support sustained performance.” **If strong drink:** “This is a strong drink. It may sharpen focus now but could increase afternoon energy drop.” **If mild drink:** “This lighter drink is a good choice for stable alertness without risk of overstimulation.” **Suggestions:** “Log drink” “Recommend a lower/higher caffeine option” “Try a non-caffeine focus activation” **SECTION 3 — TOTAL DAILY CAFFEINE MANAGEMENT** Daily intake tiers Low: \<100 mg Moderate: 100–200 mg High: 200–300 mg Very high: \>300 mg **Trigger:** User logs \>250 mg in a day OR exceeds their personalized threshold. **Primary message:** “You’re above your typical effective caffeine range for the day.” **Impact explanation:** “More caffeine now usually won’t increase focus. It’s more likely to cause anxiety, jitter, or sleep disruption.” **Suggestions:** “Try a lighter drink instead” “Use a 60-second alertness protocol” “Helpful strategies for sustaining focus without more caffeine” **SECTION 4 — SLEEP PROTECTION & LATE-DAY GUARD** **Trigger:** Drink logged within 5 hours of typical bedtime. **Primary message:** “This drink is close to your usual bedtime. Caffeine now will likely remain active when you try to sleep.” **Impact line:** “That reduces deep sleep and often leads to low clarity tomorrow morning.” **Suggestions:** “Log anyway” “Switch to a low-caffeine drink” “Do a quick alertness activation instead” | **2**                                                                                                                                | **NEUROREGULATE: NICOTINE MODULE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |                   |
|                                                                                                                                      | A neuroscience-based system designed to help users quit nicotine by dismantling the cognitive, emotional, and physiological loops that sustain dependency — with precision, stability, and autonomy. **THE CORE IDEA** Nicotine addiction is a **loop**: **Cue → Emotion/State → Nicotine → Relief → Reinforcement → Withdrawal → More Nicotine** This toolkit breaks the loop on **every layer**: **Cue Detection State Deconstruction Replacement Activation Loop Interruption Withdrawal Smoothing Behavioral Reinforcement Rebuild** Users gradually transition from: **Managing nicotine** → **Reducing nicotine** → **Eliminating nicotine** → **Building identity-level freedom** This is not willpower. It is **neural loop reprogramming**. **SECTION 1 — DEPENDENCY MAPPING & STATE ANALYSIS** We map not just “how much”, but WHY, WHEN, and WHAT STATE nicotine creates. This module creates a Nicotine Dependency Map across 7 days. **1.1 INITIAL DIAGNOSTIC (Day 1\)** User completes a guided state-map: **Prompt 1:** “When do you use nicotine most often?” **Buttons:** Morning Midday After meals Before work During stress During boredom At night Before sleep I’m not sure → app infers from logs **Prompt 2:** “What do you feel right before you reach for nicotine?” Stress Tension Lethargy / low energy Frustration Restlessness Habit / autopilot Craving in body Emotional pressure Nothing specific **Prompt 3:** “What do you feel right after nicotine?” Relief Calm Focus Reset Boost Nothing This forms the baseline profile. **1.2 DAILY USE LOGGING (simple, fast)** User logs nicotine with: Type (cigarette/pouch/vape/gum) Strength (low/medium/high) Time Reason (from short menu) **Follow-up Prompt:** “Did this give you what you expected?” Yes Partially No Made me feel worse **1.3 WEEKLY DEPENDENCY MAP (full content)** User sees: **Your Nicotine Loop Patterns:** Highest risk window: \[X:XX\] – \[X:XX\] Most common emotional trigger: \[stress / frustration / boredom\] Most destabilizing use: \[specific product\] Most reliable false reinforcement (relief lasts \<20 min): \[time pattern\] Withdrawal spike occurs at: \~\[X minutes\] after last use Nicotine interrupts your natural circadian stability at: \[X PM\] This data anchors quitting work. **2.1 EXAMPLE PROMPT** **Primary:** “We’ll gradually weaken the nicotine loop until it collapses — no willpower required.” **Secondary:** “Expect a 10–20% reduction per week with stabilization phases built in.” **2.3 QUIT PHASES (system-defined)** **Phase 1 — Loop Weakening (Days 1–7) Goals:** Delay first nicotine use by 20–60 minutes Replace 1 nicotine event a day with a physiological protocol Reduce nicotine strengths where possible **Phase 2 — Dependence Collapse (Days 8–21) Goals:** Interrupt cravings Use low-strength replacement for high-strength events Introduce Stress & Activation protocols **Phase 3 — Withdrawal Smoothing (Days 22–30) Goals:** Reduce irritability Stabilize focus Create new “break behaviors” **Phase 4 — Identity Shift (Days 30+) Goal:** Zero nicotine Daily reinforcement of new non-nicotine cues **SECTION 3 — CRAVING INTERCEPTION PROTOCOLS** Nicotine cravings peak and fade like waves.The app intercepts cravings at multiple levels. **3.1 CRAVING DETECTED PROMPT (exact)** **Primary message:** “A nicotine craving is rising. This is a conditioned response — not a need.” **Secondary line:** “The next 30–90 seconds determine whether the loop strengthens or weakens.” Options: Run 60-second Craving Interruption Replace nicotine Delay 5 minutes Log nicotine **3.2 60-SECOND CRAVING INTERRUPTION (full script)** **Step 1 — Physiological Sigh (10 sec)**“Deep inhale → small top-up → slow release. Repeat twice.” **Step 2 — Vagus Reset (10 sec)**“Exhale longer than you inhale. This reduces withdrawal tension.” **Step 3 — Somatic Displacement (15 sec)**“Press palms together firmly… release.” **Step 4 — Cognitive Deconstruction (10 sec)**“What triggered this craving?”Options: Anxiety spike Break from work Low energy Frustration Habit/autopilot Unknown **Step 5 — Reframing Line**Displayed according to selection: “This feeling is temporary — it is not a need.” “The urge will peak then drop.” “Nicotine won't fix this emotion — but this protocol already shifted your state.” **Step 6 — Action Choice** Delay 5 minutes Replace with low-strength product Skip nicotine **SECTION 4 — WITHDRAWAL STABILITY SYSTEM** Withdrawal impacts: mood focus sleep cognitive bandwidth This module smooths withdrawal intensity. **4.1 MORNING WITHDRAWAL PROMPT** **Trigger:** First unlock \+ no nicotine used yet. **Message:**“You may feel tension or irritability this morning — that’s withdrawal, not identity.” Offer: 90-second Stabilization Protocol Delay nicotine Low-strength replacement Log if using **4.2 90-SECOND WITHDRAWAL STABILIZATION PROTOCOL** **Step 1 — Long Exhale Regulation (20 sec)**“Exhale twice as long as inhale to calm autonomic activation.” **Step 2 — Chest Expansion (15 sec)**“Open the chest — improves oxygen and focus.” **Step 3 — Mindset Shift (10 sec)**“This sensation \= your brain healing.” **Step 4 — Choose:** Continue without nicotine Use a lighter product Log use **SECTION 5 — BREAK REPLACEMENT SYSTEM** Nicotine is often a “break ritual.” This module replaces the ritual without removing the break. **5.1 NICOTINE BREAK REPLACERS** User selects what type of break they want: **Break Type A — Calm Reset Prompt:**“Replace this break with a 1-minute calming ritual.” **Steps:** Breath Posture Micro-stretch Optional: water cue **Break Type B — Energy Lift Prompt:**“Replace nicotine with this activation.” **Steps:** Inhale boosts Shoulder roll Gaze sharpening **Break Type C — Emotional Shift Prompt:**“Shift state without nicotine.” **Steps:** Label emotion Reframe Release **SECTION 6 — REDUCTION FRAMEWORK** Users reduce nicotine gradually without feeling deprivation. **6.1 WEEKLY REDUCTION GOAL PROMPTS** **Week 1 Goal:**“Delay your first nicotine use by 20 minutes and replace one event each day.” **Week 2 Goal:**“Switch one high-strength nicotine use to a low-strength version.” **Week 3 Goal:**“Replace 50% of all nicotine uses.” **Week 4 Goal:**“Enter full cessation mode — the system will smooth your withdrawal.” **SECTION 7 — FULL CESSATION MODE** When user is ready to quit entirely, system shifts tone: **7.1 CESSATION DAY PROMPT Primary message:**“Today your body begins healing. Expect intensity — it will pass.” **Secondary:**“Your withdrawal stabilization protocols will activate automatically at the right times.” **7.2 STABILITY SCHEDULE Morning:** Withdrawal smoother**Late Morning:** Craving buffer**Afternoon:** Energy reset**Evening:** Emotional stabilizer \+ sleep support **7.3 CESSATION DAY MILESTONES & Prompts Hour 1:**“You’ve begun the reset. Withdrawal is your brain recalibrating.” **Hour 8:**“Nicotine levels drop sharply here. Let’s stabilize your state.” **Hour 24:**“Most nicotine is out. Cravings now are habit loops, not chemical.” **SECTION 8 — IDENTITY REBUILD & FREEDOM MODE** Once nicotine is removed: **8.1 IDENTITY SHIFT PROMPTS Daily Morning Prompt:**“You are operating nicotine-free. Your nervous system is rebuilding clarity.” **Random Reinforcement Prompt:**“You handled a difficult moment without nicotine — this is how loops permanently break.” **Weekly Summary:**“You’ve rebuilt your baseline state without nicotine. This is long-term freedom.” [NeuroAtlas](https://www.figma.com/design/JFNkMTXg35AhyJ2aXuzeFA/NeuroAtlas?node-id=1432-4126&t=4pRZeOoIn2exjOGJ-1) | **3**                                                                                                                                | **SEDENTARY RESET**
